name: Ahdoos
why_it_matters: Started 1918 as a bakery by Haji Mohammad Sultan, who trained in Kolkata under Maharaja Hari Singh's patronage; by the 1920s it was the first restaurant in the Valley to serve full Kashmiri Wazwan. Still family-run from the same Residency Road frontage.
insider_tip: Order the half-wazwan if there are two of you — a full wazwan is built for four and the rice alone defeats most travellers. Bakerkhani from the attached bakery downstairs is the morning move.
signature_address: Lal Chowk Market, Ahdoos Hotel, Residency Road, Srinagar 190001

name: Mughal Darbar
why_it_matters: Started in 1984 by Haji Mohammad Ibrahim Mugloo as a fast-food shop and grew into the second wazwan name on Residency Road after Ahdoos. Harissa here in winter (the slow-cooked mutton-and-rice breakfast porridge) is the local trip people make from across town.
insider_tip: If wazwan feels heavy, order the harissa with kandur tchot bread between November and February — it is not on the standard menu but the kitchen serves it from a separate counter in the morning.

name: Stream Restaurant
signature_dish: wazwan thali with Dal Lake view
why_it_matters: The Boulevard end's stand-alone wazwan room — opposite Ghat No. 2, looking straight onto Dal Lake. Tripadvisor's perennial top-ranked Srinagar restaurant; locals quietly admit the view earns part of that ranking, but the wazwan thali is honest work.
insider_tip: Ask for a window table on the Dal-facing side at booking — they exist but are not assigned by default. Sunset thali is the moment; the kitchen winds down by 9:30pm.
signature_address: Boulevard Road, Opposite Ghat No. 2, near PNB Bank, Dal Gate, Srinagar 190001

name: Tao Cafe
why_it_matters: An open-garden continental cafe on Residency Road opposite the GPO since 1983 — predates the cafe wave by three decades. Where Srinagar businesspeople and visiting journalists have parked between Lal Chowk meetings for forty years.
insider_tip: Outdoor garden seats fill by 1pm in summer; the indoor room is air-conditioned but loses the point. Cash works faster than card — the card machine is moody.

name: Chai Jaai
why_it_matters: First-floor tea room above Mahattas Studio on the Bund, looking onto the Jhelum — modelled on the Cotswold tea-room template but built around Kashmiri kahwa, noon chai, and the samovar tradition. The single best place in central Srinagar to taste both teas back-to-back, served properly.
insider_tip: Order kahwa first, noon chai second — the salty pink tea will overwrite the kahwa's saffron-almond finish if you reverse the order. Ask for a window seat over the river.
signature_address: 1st Floor, Mahattas Studio, The Bund Road, Munshi Bagh, Srinagar 190001

name: Cafe 99 Polo View
why_it_matters: First-floor cafe in Polo Plaza on the Polo View pedestrian street — Srinagar's smartest open-air shopping spine since the 2022 pedestrianisation. Mid-range pizza-and-pasta with reliable Wi-Fi, a calmer alternative to the chaos of Residency Road.
insider_tip: Polo View itself is the actual draw — book this cafe as a halfway break between the carpet showrooms and the silver shops, not as a destination dinner. Lunch buffet pricing is sharper than à la carte.
signature_address: 1st Floor, Polo Plaza, Polo View, Lal Chowk, Srinagar 190001

name: Cafe De Polo
why_it_matters: First-floor cafe with a balcony overlooking the Polo View promenade — the cleanest sit-down coffee on the strip if Cafe 99 is full. Useful as a meeting spot since the area is pedestrian and Polo View itself is the address most locals navigate by.
insider_tip: The balcony seats over the street are the only ones worth queuing for; indoor seating loses the entire point of the location. Coffee is decent, the food menu is broader than the kitchen can deliver consistently.
signature_address: 1st Floor, Polo View, M.A. Road, Lal Chowk, Srinagar 190001

name: Parsa's
why_it_matters: Founded by Javid Parsa in October 2017 in a 200-sqft Sarah Mall kiosk on Rs 7 lakh of Amazon-job savings; now 38 outlets across the Valley, Jammu, Delhi, Bengaluru and Kargil. The Lal Chowk original is still where the kathi roll recipe was set.
insider_tip: The chicken kathi roll is the dish that built the brand; the biryani is competent but not why people queue. Skip the breakfast slot — the rolls peak in the late-afternoon batch.
signature_address: Sarah City Center, near Jehangir Chowk, Airport (IG) Road, Lal Chowk, Srinagar 190001

name: Cafe Liberty
why_it_matters: Heritage-styled cafe near the old Liberty Cinema corner of M.A. Road — bark-clad walls, vintage radios, ski sets, old film posters and antique doors curated as a deliberate Kashmir-time-capsule fitout. Feels like the answer to 'where do young Srinagaris hang out now'.
insider_tip: The food is fine, the room is the reason — order kahwa and a kebab platter, not a full meal. Closes earlier on Fridays for the afternoon prayer break; check before walking over.
signature_address: 309 Alijan Shopping Complex, M.A. Road, Lal Chowk, Srinagar 190001

name: Lhasa Restaurant
why_it_matters: Opened 1976 by the late Abdul Rehman Zareif as the first restaurant in the Valley to serve Chinese and Tibetan food — momos and thukpa were essentially introduced to Srinagar from this kitchen. Set in a quiet garden lane off Boulevard Road, between two Dal Lake ghats.
insider_tip: The fried momos are what locals order — steamed momos are competent but the kitchen's fryer is the Lhasa speciality. Garden seating is functional rather than scenic; come for the food, not the view.
signature_address: Lane No. 3, Boulevard Road, Opposite Ghat No. 9, near New Park Hotel, Dal Gate, Srinagar 190001
